summary: A mundane building obstruction shows Carrie that one male Kin and the Upstairs Neighbor already coordinate without her mediation.

panelPlan.action: Wide. A boxed mattress delivery has been left diagonally in the narrow hall, partly blocking the stairs. The Upstairs Neighbor is annoyed. The first male Kin is already at one end of the box.
Carrie and Bjorn arrive from the stairs. Carrie opens her mouth to organize.
Neighbor points.
They pivot the box together cleanly around the landing, using gestures and a few familiar words. Carrie never gets a sentence in.
Carrie watches them disappear upstairs with the mattress.

dialogueInline.text: Up, not down.
Up.
You were going to help.
I was going to be very helpful.

summary: Silas hears the word review and reflexively designs a public campaign, then recognizes that he is trying to become narrator again.

panelPlan.action: Wide. Silas stands just inside 5B with phone, tablet, and too much energy. Carrie has made the mistake of mentioning the review.
Bjorn stares at him. Gunnar keeps reading.
Silas catches his own reflection in the dark phone screen and slows.
Carrie.
Silas puts the phone face down.

dialogueInline.text: Okay. We can do neighborhood testimonials, a short-form series, maybe one hero piece—
I'm doing the thing again.
Very much.
Fine. What boring thing actually needs doing?

summary: Carrie gives Silas a narrow administrative task, and he completes it without turning the household into content.

panelPlan.action: Medium. Carrie's old compact printer jams on the review-notice copies. Silas is already reaching for a grander solution.
Carrie points at printer.
Insert. Silas opens the printer, removes a crumpled sheet, reseats the tray. Ordinary tech repair, no hacker visuals.
Medium. Two clean copies feed out.
Silas hands them over and looks visibly tempted to say more.

dialogueInline.text: I can scan everything into a shared—
Make that produce two readable pages.
Done.
Thank you.
I have several thoughts.
I know.

summary: The table fills with objects that point toward the household's life, and Bjorn refuses to let those objects substitute for the people who use them.

panelPlan.action: Top-down table composition. Brass key, Gunnar's library card and book, laundry ticket, transit card, bodega receipt, Carrie's review notice, a small household tool.
Carrie arranges only the items genuinely relevant to the review.
Bjorn looks at the collection.
Carrie meets his eyes.
She deliberately moves the objects aside to clear seats around the table.

dialogueInline.text: This is enough to establish continuity of residence and independent activity.
These are not us.
I know.
They're how paper points at a life. They are not the life.

summary: Bjorn asks Gunnar and the two male Kin what each actually wants, and the answers remain visibly different instead of being synthesized into one household doctrine.
settingText: Safe Cave table, early evening; Astrid is still out.

panelPlan.action: Bjorn sits with Carrie, Gunnar and the two male Kin. The brass key, transit card and review notice are present but pushed to the side rather than arranged as symbols.
First Male Kin answers from the practical life already established around the building and block.
Gunnar answers without looking at the review notice.
Second Male Kin turns the transit card once between his fingers before answering.
Bjorn looks from one man to the next, dissatisfied that the answers do not combine neatly. Carrie leaves that discomfort unresolved.

dialogueInline.text: Say what you want.
This room. This block. The people who know us.
The library. The city. Places I have not seen yet.
I want to stay. I do not know after.
Those are not one answer.
Then don't make them one tonight.

summary: Carrie tries to anticipate the hearing's questions, but the household discovers that knowing what each person wants is not the same as knowing how the institution will frame those wants.
settingText: Same Safe Cave table, continuing the evening council.

panelPlan.action: Carrie turns the review notice around and points to several broad categories without reading them as a speech.
Gunnar looks at the paper and then back at Carrie.
Second Male Kin leans back, visibly irritated by the idea of rehearsing certainty.
Bjorn dislikes the lack of a common prepared answer; Carrie refuses to manufacture one for them.
Nobody writes a household statement. The review notice remains open, unanswered in several places.

dialogueInline.text: They may ask about residence, independence, intention, household ties.
Those are four questions again.
And they may not mean what we mean.
I dislike entering judgment without a plan.
A plan is fine. Rehearsed answers are not.
Then let them ask.
